correctness.rationale: A geometric fixed point has orbit-constant barycentric weights; selecting internally independent vertex orbits produces exactly an independence complex of the orbit-adjacency graph. Nontrivial label cycles are excluded at the top clique. An open-neighborhood inclusion folds each nontrivial orbit vertex against a fixed-label singleton whenever f>=1. With f=0 all same-level orbit vertices are twins and collapse to a path. The standard path recurrence and published integral wedge theorem establish all infinite-parameter homotopy types. A standalone independently reconstructing checker confirms 117 graph reductions, 37 signed Lefschetz sums, and 28 full small F2 homology computations; no finite check is substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The theorem gives constructive integral homotopy types of every geometric label-permutation fixed space of an infinite and recently studied family; the collapse depends only on number of fixed labels even when nontrivial cycle structures vary. Derangements exhibit a nontrivial depth-three periodic sphere/contractible transition. Prior nonequivariant Betti ranks and rational characters do not determine these spaces or their simple-homotopy reductions, making this a structural fixed-point invariant of value in equivariant topology.
